_note: Two 1-3 cm meshes sitting at plus and minus 7.36 m on a 14.80 m span - the wingtips, to within 4 cm of the half-span. Wingtip lights. They were classified as tail because they are small, paired and far off the centreline, which is also what a tailplane looks like to a bounding box. Left as tail they stayed behind when the wing came off, hanging seven metres out in clear air: the widest gap in the whole geometry sweep, at 37% of the aircraft's length.
_note_tail: Reclassifying those two left the Predator with no tail mesh at all, and its real inverted-V tail is welded into the fuselage boom - so the tail is a cut. Measured with scripts/measure-region.py rather than guessed: along the length axis the aft 17% carries geometry reaching plus and minus 0.226 of the half-span and the full height of the hull, which is the V-tail, while the boom immediately forward of it is only 0.049 wide. Keeping a 0.06 band therefore keeps the boom and drops both tail surfaces. aftSign is unaffected (still 1), so station, CG and static margin are unchanged.

tail.comment: keeps the 0.36 m boom out of a 7.4 m half-span and drops the inverted-V surfaces outboard of it, in the aft 1.5 m only
